A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FP4DiT and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization evaluations, human preference studies, ablations, generated-image comparisons, and hardware latency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds ImageReward measurements, calibration-size and guidance-scale analyses, and qualitative baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The mixed floating-point formats, scale-aware AdaRound objectives and updates, group-wise weight quantization, and online token-wise activation quantization are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS-COCO, HPSv2, and the existing text-to-image prompt studies. The new measurements, parameter sweeps, and replacement illustrative example remain within the retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The quantitative and human-study comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v3 adds Q-DiT to the PixArt qualitative comparisons in Figures 11–14 and adds both ViDiT-Q and Q-DiT to the Hunyuan comparisons in Figures 15–16.

E3.justification: v3 adds ImageReward evaluation on COCO outputs and introduces calibration-size sweeps over 64, 128, 256, and 512 samples and CFG tests at 3.0, 4.5, and 7.0 after calibration at 4.5. Existing main-experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2.2–A.2.3 analyses test calibration-data requirements and robustness to changing CFG on PixArt-α. Existing component, calibration-budget, and group-size ablations remain. Qualitative comparisons are expanded, and Figure 7 replaces its northern-lights example with a portrait.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the performance comparisons. The human-study participant counts and existing distribution plots are retained; the new results follow the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All previously reported Table 2 scores are unchanged. v3 adds ImageReward scores, calibration-size and CFG results, and qualitative outputs. The new Hunyuan W4A6 ImageReward results favor Q-DiT over FP4DiT, −1.1822 versus −1.7880. Appendix A.2.2 reports 27.43 and 28.21 HPSv2 for 128 and 256 calibration samples.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations 1–12, and both scale-aware AdaRound theorems and proofs in Appendix A.1 are retained. Differences are typographical or positional rather than changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion explicitly extend the comparative performance claims to ImageReward. The central W4A6/W4A8 capability claims and contributions concerning mixed formats, scale-aware rounding, and activation quantization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds hypotheses connecting ImageReward degradation to image resolution and perceptual sensitivity, and acknowledges the Hunyuan W4A6 ImageReward exception. It also interprets the new appendix results as supporting small calibration sets and robustness across CFG scales.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit FP4DiT repository link and adds batch size 2, 4096 tokens, and embedding dimension 1152 to the latency-table caption. These are additional disclosures; the existing hardware and calibration hyperparameters remain unchanged, with old Table 10 becoming Table 12.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work broaden the efficiency context to pruning, sparsification, and distillation, and add citations including QuIP, SpinQuant, and ImageReward. The central positioning relative to U-Net quantization and text-to-image DiT research is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized revisions to the introduction, related work, results discussion, conclusion, and appendix prose, and updates affiliations and publication information. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The qualitative presentation is substantially revised: Figures 11–14 expand from five to six comparison rows, Figures 15–16 from four to six, and Figure 7 replaces its PixArt-Σ example. Higher-resolution graphics, descriptive panel labels in Figures 4–5, an ImageReward column, and two new appendix tables further change the displays.

improvement.justification: The added ImageReward measurements, sensitivity analyses, fuller qualitative comparisons, and explicit code and latency details modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gains are limited by Table 10 incorrectly labeling every calibration-size column N=64 and by retaining an all-metrics superiority statement despite the acknowledged Hunyuan ImageReward exception. The core method and existing quantitative results remain unchanged.
